lines.say: Evening. Anything going on round here?
lines.reply: Quiet night. Same as most nights this time of year.

lines.say: You look like you've been stood there a while.
lines.reply: Been on since half six.

lines.say: What are you selling today, then?
lines.reply: Nothing you can name, that's the thing.

lines.say: How long have you kept the books for Mickey?
lines.reply: Thirty-one years. Since before you were born, most likely.

lines.say: Did you hear the glass go last night?
lines.reply: You've had the lot off me, friend.

lines.say: Who's the new owner, then?
lines.reply: Fella called Nowak.

lines.say: Is it always this quiet on a Tuesday?
lines.reply: Tuesdays are market day.

lines.say: Were you on the docks, before?
lines.reply: Thirty years. Till eighty-nine, when they let us go. Mickey kept me on after that, kept me on the rank here. Been here ever since.

lines.say: Can you get me a pager?
lines.reply: So listen, I might know somebody who knows somebody. But a pager's not the sort of thing you just walk into a shop and come out with, you know? Takes time, takes money upfront. What's it worth to you?

lines.say: Do you know who broke the window?
lines.reply: What window?

lines.say: Cold one tonight, isn't it.
lines.reply: Rain's coming on before morning. You can feel it in the air.

lines.say: Your mum know you're out?
lines.reply: That's the lot, honest. I'd tell you if there was more.

lines.say: Evening. Anything going on round here?
lines.reply: You're back. No. Same as before you left.

lines.say: You look like you've been stood there a while.
lines.reply: You've had the lot off me, friend.

lines.say: What are you selling today, then?
lines.reply: Look, I told you that already. Nothing you can name. But if something comes up, something you need, something you heard about, I'm the one who knows who to ask. That's what I sell, innit. Information, a favour, a connection. Right now there's not much moving, but there's always something.

lines.say: How long have you kept the books for Mickey?
lines.reply: I've already told you that. Thirty-one years.

lines.say: Did you hear the glass go last night?
lines.reply: What glass, boss? Nothing came to me on the rank last night. Street was quiet enough.

lines.say: Who's the new owner, then?
lines.reply: I said, Nowak. Came in after Mickey passed, what, three weeks after? One suitcase and a letter saying the place was his. Living up in Mickey's flat now.

lines.say: Is it always this quiet on a Tuesday?
lines.reply: Quiet night. Same as most nights this time of year.

lines.say: Were you on the docks, before?
lines.reply: Thirty years on the quay.
